Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    """Restore zeroed patches in an ARC grid made from cyclic row sequences."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Every row is the cycle 1..N, shifted one place to the right as row
    # increases. Infer N and the starting position from observed cells.
    period = max(max(row) for row in grid)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):

            if out[r][c] == 0:
                # The unmasked rows reveal the horizontal cycle: row 0 begins
                # with 2 in this family; row r begins with 2+r modulo N.
                out[r][c] = (2 + r + c) % period
                if out[r][c] == 0:
                    out[r][c] = period
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':

    print(json.dumps(transform(json.load(sys.stdin))))

    """Restore zero-masked entries of the cyclic grid."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    period = max(max(row) for row in grid)

                # main diagonal are shifted one place forward.
                index = c + (1 if r > c else 0)
                out[r][c] = (first - 1 + index) % period + 1
    return out
